name: Aqara Camera Hub G3 (EU)

radios.note: Dual-band 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi and a built-in Zigbee 3.0 hub.

matter.note: Aqara's G3 pages we saw name HomeKit, Alexa and Google Home but not Matter; no CSA listing was checked.

apple_home.note: Supports HomeKit Secure Video. In that mode recording drops to 1080p and pan/tilt control is not available. Needs an Apple home hub for HSV.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Google Home and says the G3 is exposed to it as a camera only. Whether live view works on Nest Hub displays was not confirmed.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Alexa and says the G3 is exposed as a camera only. Whether live view works on Echo Show was not confirmed.

smartthings.note: No Aqara or Samsung page we found mentions SmartThings for the G3.

home_assistant.note: Reachable only through a community integration (Aqara Open API) or HomeKit pairing per third-party pages; no official Home Assistant docs found.

hubRequired.note: The G3 is itself a Zigbee hub for Aqara sensors; it needs no separate hub.

localControl.note: Aqara says face, gesture and pet recognition and storage in the Aqara Home app run locally; local-only control is not stated.

cameraType.note: Pan/tilt indoor camera hub; the indoor-only wording was not seen in snippets.

localStorage.note: microSD card, not included; class 4 or above, up to 128 GB.

subscription.value: None for Aqara storage; iCloud+ for HSV
subscription.note: Aqara says third-party cloud storage such as HomeKit Secure Video may need a paid plan. No Aqara plan was found in snippets.

summary: The Aqara Camera Hub G3 is an indoor pan/tilt camera with 2K (2304 x 1296) video that doubles as a Zigbee 3.0 hub for Aqara sensors. It records to a microSD card of up to 128 GB and runs face, gesture and pet recognition on the device. Apple Home (with HomeKit Secure Video), Google Home and Alexa are listed by Aqara. SmartThings and Home Assistant support are not confirmed.
caveats: HomeKit Secure Video limits recording to 1080p and disables pan/tilt control.
Google Home and Alexa see it as a camera only, not as a Zigbee hub.
Retailers disagree on how many Zigbee devices it supports (64 vs 128); Aqara's page does not state a number.
A HomeKit pairing is exclusive, so it cannot sit in Apple Home and another HomeKit controller at once.
